## TL;DR
`repoos restart` restarts this repo's server whether it is a RepoOS service, an external launchd/systemd supervisor (including system-domain LaunchDaemons, the Kamrai case) or hand-run, with accurate warnings and failure guidance. This round fixes review pass 5.

## Work and rationale
- `src/core/service-manager.ts`: `repoosBinary()`, `generatePlist()` and `generateUnit()` again resolve the compiled CLI entry through the shared `compiledCliEntry()` helper. The previous round had inlined `dirname(dirname(import.meta.url))` here, which from `dist/core/` computes `dist/` and then joins a *second* `dist/`, yielding `dist/dist/cli/index.js` — the pass-2 bug, re-introduced. The helper is dist/core-safe (checks the real parent first, then the repo root) and is already covered by `serve-lock-flags.test.ts`. A new regression test in `service-manager.test.ts` forces the no-PATH fallback (a `which` that exits 1) and asserts `repoosBinary()` returns a `needsCliEntry` interpreter plus an existing entry that is not `dist/dist`; the test fails on the broken inline form.
- Reverted `restartCommand` in `src/core/service-manager.ts` (and its test) to main's behaviour: when the server is DOWN, the banner hint is `repoos serve --port N`, because `repoos restart` refuses when nothing is listening. The `/api/health` field and the offline banner are unchanged.
- `user-docs/troubleshooting.md`: the "Not running" bullet again says to start the server; `repoos restart` is documented for a running or stale server.
- The uncertain-supervisor refusal now prints a single `kill <pid>` step with a note that it only stops the server and what to run if nothing answers; it no longer prints `kill && serve`, which could race a supervisor's respawn onto the same port. Test updated.
- Earlier rounds on the branch: system-domain `launchctl print`, `managed` kind, pid always verified, managed-port match, shutdown warning listing all in-flight work, stop-then-start failure messages, external-supervisor and classification tests.

## Approaches tried
Making `repoos restart` start a server when none is found was rejected as scope creep; keeping the down-state hint as `repoos serve` preserves the #0959 contract.

## Challenges and blockers
No live non-sudo KeepAlive LaunchDaemon respawn test was possible; detection is covered by fixtures that mirror `launchctl print system` rows.

## Key learnings
A hint shown while the server is down must start it, not restart it. A bare `kill` is never a restart. And a dist-path helper has to live in exactly one place: three inline copies of `dirname(dirname(import.meta.url))` is how `dist/dist` came back.
